title: Hawk Talks, The Mooch and Murder at the Vanities
summary: Willard lists more films; Tizol remembers only playing Hawk Talks.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: With the band. Yeah, I think I have the record. There's another short listed here; another three minute one. It was done of "Hawk Talks." ""

" Hawk Talks. " The Hot Tots -- Louie Bellson's number, remember, that he wrote? He wrote that in Harry's band, right, and then took it and Duke recorded it. He took it with him when he moved to Duke's band.
" Hawk Talks "? Remember the tune, the Hot Tots?
Yeah, we played it with Duke Ellington, yeah.

Yeah. Well, apparently, you made a three minute film of it, playing it. In fact, I think I've seen that one with Duke's band -- and you're in it, doing " Hawk Talks, " the Hot Tots, and you made a lot of films; probably more than you realize.

And then there's another three minute short of " The Mooch " that you were on, done in 1952, and at the same time, " Moon Indigo " with Duke, a short film. And then, in 1934, here is one you didn't mention -- " Murder at the Vanities ", remember that?
That was where the band played Ebony Rhapsody.
That's a little too far back for me.
It was a comedy, murder mystery. they showed it up here at the Vagabond Theatre a few months ago.

And the whole band -- Duke has a few lines in it, and the whole band got a lot of film space -- Toby, Harry, Johnny, Barney, Freddie Jenkins, Cootie, Arthur Whetsol, Tricky Sam, and you, Lawrence, Freddie Guy, Wellman Braud, Sonny Greer and Duke.
Sometimes that's on television, too -- if you ever see Murder at the Vanities, you can get a glimpse of yourself.
